title: The Orpheus Group
summary: A company that sends agents among the dead.

claims.text: Project Echo is the Group's work on finding, making and using projectors.
Its agents have their own slang; its researchers coin more technical words, and agent slang is far more common.
A horror show is an illegal job in which a client pays Orpheus to frighten a target into madness or a possibly fatal accident.
A beach is a break between missions, usually a week or more; a snow job is a mission that looks too easy.
A fumigation is a mission to clear a place of spooks, usually by destroying them.

title: Projectors
summary: Living people whose spirits can leave the body.

claims.text: A projector is a living human whose spirit can leave the body and travel.
Skimmers project by yogic technique; going zero is leaving the body, and ripcording is snapping back at once, which harms the body and is kept for desperate escapes.
Sleepers are agents who have been flatlined and kept in cryogenic suspension; their tubes are cradles, or coffins.
The body a projector leaves behind is called the meat. Death merchants are freelance mercenary projectors.

title: Ghosts: Spirits and Hues
summary: The two kinds of ghost among the player Laments.

claims.text: Ghosts are spooks who do not project. Spirits are the common kind; hues used pigment in life and differ from spirits.
Spook covers ghosts and projectors alike, anyone in gauze or without a body.
Drones are ghosts with Vitality 1, called repeaters; blips have 2 or 3 and are near-functional, called reactives.
Jasons are living people taken over by mad spooks or Spectres who then kill like serial killers.

title: Laments
summary: A character's kind of ghost or projector.

claims.text: A Lament is a character's race: ghost or projector, each with two subsets.
Laments decide much less of a character than Nature and role do; each character is meant to stay an individual.

title: Shades
summary: The five templates that shape a ghost's outlook.

claims.text: The five Shades are the Banshee, the Haunter, the Poltergeist, the Skinrider and the Will-o-the-Wisp.
Agent slang: a Banshee is a screamer, a Haunter a squatter, a Poltergeist a breaker, a Skinrider a control freak or puppetmaster, a Wisp a flicker.
Someone a Skinrider rides or controls is called a Malkovich.

title: Vitality
summary: A spook's life force and body at once.

claims.text: Vitality and Spite are the two central traits of every character.
A spook's body is the projection of its soul's emotional state, so Vitality is both its energy and its body.
Sharing Vitality within a crucible is called networking.

title: Spite and Stains
summary: The darkness that builds in a spook.

claims.text: Spite is the negative energy and feeling that gathers in a spook's soul.
When Spite rises above Vitality, the character starts slipping away from the person they think they are.
Stains are changes to the ghostly form when insecurity and fear warp the sense of self; each makes the character less human.
Stains come to those who often give way to rage or bitterness, but they often give some protection or advantage.

title: Horrors
summary: The powers of ghosts and projectors.

claims.text: Horrors are the powers projectors and ghosts use.
Thorns are a Spectre's innate powers.
Special effects, or F/X, is agent code for any Horror or Stain in public.
Manifesting is appearing to and acting on the living.

title: Pigment
summary: A new street drug tied to the dead.

claims.text: Pigment, also called black heroin, is a cheap, addictive hallucinogen popular with casual users such as students and ravers.
Pigment addicts are deadheads, and agents dislike them because they seem able to see spooks.

title: Crucible
summary: A team of spooks working together.

claims.text: A crucible is a circle of ghosts and projectors whose different aims are made to work together.
Crucibles usually have high Vitality. A rave is a fight among several spooks; the Big Bad is a powerful spook leading others or controlling living people.

title: The Shroud and the Wastelands
summary: What lies beyond death, as the living understand it.

claims.text: The Shroud is the veil between this world and the one thought to lie past it; some call it the Stormwall.
The Wastelands are a rumoured land of the dead being torn apart by the Maelstrom on the far side of the Shroud.
The Maelstrom was a great event some years ago that swept many ghosts away; little is known of it but rumour.
The Nothing is a ghost rumour of what follows a ghost's utter destruction; there is no evidence either way.
Gauze, or plasm, is a spook's body; the Quick are the living.

title: The Orpheus Series
summary: A limited game told in a set run of books.

claims.text: The game is a limited run that builds like a suspense film, each supplement a new revelation toward a final climax.
The run goes Crusade of Ashes, Shades of Gray, Shadow Games, The Orphan-Grinders, and End Game.

title: Banshee
summary: The Shade that hears past, present and future.

claims.text: Banshees read what has passed, mediate what is happening and foresee what will come, following other people's feelings to old pain.

title: Haunter
summary: The Shade of haunted places and cursed things.

claims.text: The Shade draws on tales found worldwide of haunted places and cursed items, such as the Tower of London, the Amityville house and the cursed objects of Tutankhamen's tomb.

title: Poltergeist
summary: The Shade of the angry spirit.

claims.text: The angry ghost that hurls its rage at the living, often tied to a place or object it knew in life, is the classic Poltergeist.

title: Skinrider
summary: The Shade that rides the living.

claims.text: Skinriders work Horrors of Puppetry, taking the bodies of the living.

title: Wisp
summary: The Shade of strange lights and lulls.

claims.text: Among Wisp Horrors is Unearthly Repose, which can put even alert, well-caffeinated guards to sleep.

title: Investigative Consulting
summary: The core of Orpheus's business.

claims.text: Investigative Consultants handle the daily work, which ranges from routine sales calls up to speaking with the recently dead.

title: Orpheus Leadership
summary: The executives at the top.

claims.text: A small Executive Leadership Team brings over 125 years of combined senior management at firms of similar size.

title: Post-Life Entities
summary: The company word for ghosts.

claims.text: Orpheus Group calls what others would name a ghost a post-life entity, or PLE.
The PLE monitor is a handheld detector the size of a PDA, with only 30 minutes of battery and other compromises made to keep it portable.

title: Zero Vitality
summary: When a ghost runs dry.

claims.text: A character at zero Vitality is utterly exhausted and cannot move whatever the danger, much like climbers stranded high on Everest.

title: Starting Spite
summary: How Spite begins.

claims.text: Starting Spite is the Shade's Base Spite plus the Spite modifier of the chosen Nature.
Draining Vitality from a ghost can raise Spite.

title: Spectres
summary: The most dangerous foes a crucible meets.

claims.text: A Spectre is to an ordinary ghost what a serial killer is to an average person; it was once human like other ghosts.
Orpheus knows that ghosts can become Spectres, and that the bodily changes many ghosts and projectors show, called Stains, grow far worse when they do.

title: Lost Boys
summary: Spectres born of neglect.

claims.text: Named for the children of Peter Pan, Lost Boys were children who died through their parents' criminal neglect, so beaten down that Spectrehood was a short fall.

title: Frighteners
summary: Spectres born of violent death.

claims.text: A Frightener is made by a death so violent it drives the person straight into Spectrehood, full of helpless rage at how it happened.

title: Fetches
summary: The Spectres' hounds.

claims.text: Fetches hunt powerful ghosts and projectors who might interfere with Spectres; a large spend of Vitality usually brings a Fetch.

title: Reapers
summary: Spectral assassins.

claims.text: Reapers are the strongest Spectres Orpheus has met: subtle, brutally efficient assassins who remove ghostly threats.

title: Terrel & Squib
summary: Orpheus's chief rival.

claims.text: Terrel & Squib, a drug company, is Orpheus Group's chief rival; its scientific respectability and its policy of putting clients first and asking nothing draw customers who avoid Orpheus.

title: NextWorld Inc.
summary: A rival born of Soviet research.

claims.text: NextWorld's roots lie in Cold War Soviet military experiments with psychic powers and the paranormal, run by the GRU.

title: The Midnight Star
summary: A believer's crusade for proof.

claims.text: Michael Sloane, a recent true believer, spends part of a fortune on scientific proof of the paranormal and on spreading the message widely.

title: The Black Steel Centipede Triad
summary: A crime empire that deals with ghosts.

claims.text: The triad is a private criminal empire under Zong Hong-fu, among the most feared crime lords in Asia, and will take on nearly any crime or vice.

title: Amateurs and Independents
summary: Freelance ghost hunters.

claims.text: Independent investigators vary too widely to sum up: one might be a doctor of mathematics or a Cherokee medicine man, or both.

title: Radio Free Death
summary: A nightly broadcast from somewhere.

claims.text: Every night at midnight someone broadcasts through a satellite TV provider from the chronicle's home city; that the source is a ghost of some kind seems likely.
